_meta.spec: EMCA Decision Engine - label rules (sibling of OVCA_Decision_Engine_Spec_v0.1 §4; same record shape)
_meta.hard_rule: Every rule below was read from the retrieved label text via the DailyMed SPL v2 API (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/services/v2/spls/{setid}.xml). No rule was reconstructed from memory. Only Indications (§1, for indication wording), Dosage and Administration (§2) and Contraindications (§4) were read; Warnings (§5) and Boxed Warnings were not extracted for the new records.
_meta.reused_from_ovca: 16 records copied verbatim from ovca-decision-engine data/labels.json (carboplatin, cisplatin, paclitaxel, topotecan, bevacizumab, olaparib, niraparib, pembrolizumab, trastuzumab_deruxtecan) and data/labels_histotypes.json (nivolumab, ipilimumab, durvalumab, lenvatinib, letrozole, trastuzumab, ifosfamide); fetched 2026-10-05, not re-fetched.
_meta.fetched_today: 15 labels fetched 2026-10-06 by tools/fetch_labels.py: dostarlimab (JEMPERLI), atezolizumab (TECENTRIQ IV), doxorubicin (conventional, Pfizer), cyclophosphamide (Baxter), medroxyprogesterone_acetate (PROVERA), megestrol_acetate (Teva tablets), tamoxifen (Mylan tablets), everolimus (AFINITOR), selinexor (XPOVIO), sacituzumab_govitecan (TRODELVY), pazopanib (VOTRIENT), dasatinib (SPRYCEL), temsirolimus (TORISEL), ixabepilone (IXEMPRA), filgrastim (NEUPOGEN).
_meta.retrieved: 31 of 34 keys have a label (16 reused + 15 new).
_meta.failed: sacituzumab_tirumotecan (no DailyMed SPL - not FDA-approved), adavosertib (investigational, no SPL). aspirin deliberately not fetched (OTC monograph; no prescription USPI dose-modification section).
_meta.off_label_warning: Of the new labels only JEMPERLI (dostarlimab) and megestrol acetate tablets carry an endometrial-cancer indication. PROVERA's indications exclude uterine cancer and its §4 lists estrogen- or progesterone-dependent neoplasia; the label doses (5-10 mg) do not cover the 200-600 mg/day used in EC. All other new agents are off-label in EC, so their dose tables are for the labelled indications.
_meta.ctcae_version_warning: Label grade scales differ: JEMPERLI and VOTRIENT use CTCAE v5.0; TECENTRIQ Table 3 uses CTCAE v4 (as does KEYTRUDA); IXEMPRA Table 1 uses CTCAE v3.0; TORISEL cites NCI CTCAE without version; AFINITOR, XPOVIO, TRODELVY, SPRYCEL do not restate the version in §2. Grade thresholds are copied as printed.
_meta.field_note: Contraindications are stored as 'baseline_contraindications' (the OVCA field name the ranker reads). Extra field 'label_indication' records indication wording where it matters for EC (on/off-label).

cisplatin.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, CISPLATIN FOR INJECTION [WG Critical Care], SPL v4, updated 2026-07-06, effectiveTime 20260624, setid 508496cb-3441-46b3-a4fe-e0d440e6adc6

cisplatin.notes: IMPORTANT DIVERGENCE: the PLR label's §2.5 is three sentences with NO numeric thresholds. The older non-PLR generic label (CISPLATIN INJECTION [Hikma], setid 76aea034-6d58-4390-a164-36aa09c1f101, updated 2025-11-20) DOES carry numeric retreatment thresholds: repeat course withheld until serum creatinine <1.5 mg/100 mL and/or BUN <25 mg/100 mL; until platelets >=100,000/mm3 and WBC >=4,000/mm3; and until audiometry shows auditory acuity within normal limits. That older label also contraindicates pre-existing renal impairment, myelosuppression and hearing impairment. If the engine needs actionable numeric cisplatin thresholds they come only from the older-format label - version the two separately.

trastuzumab_deruxtecan.notes: CTCAE v5.0. The ILD rule is sharply asymmetric and is the key gate for the spec's baseline_risk.ild_or_pneumonitis: grade 1 permits interruption and rechallenge, but ANY symptomatic (>=grade 2) ILD mandates permanent discontinuation. The LVEF ladder is what baseline_risk.cardiac_lvef_low should key off. Dose-reduction schedule differs between gastric (6.4 start) and breast/NSCLC/IHC 3+ (5.4 start) - OVCA HER2 3+ use follows the 5.4 ladder.

dosage modification printed as '75%' in Table 1 (read as a 75% dose reduction - see notes)

rules.ae: elevated serum total bilirubin / severe hepatic impairment

rules.grade_threshold: burning or stinging sensation or other evidence of peri-venous infiltration or extravasation
rules.action: stop the ongoing injection immediately; do not remove needle until aspiration attempted, do not flush, intermittent ice 15 min 4x/day for 3 days, elevate limb, consider dexrazoxane in adults

baseline_contraindications: severe myocardial insufficiency (§4)
recent (within the past 4-6 weeks) myocardial infarction (§4)
severe persistent drug-induced myelosuppression (§4)
severe hepatic impairment - Child-Pugh C or serum bilirubin >5 mg/dL (§4)
severe hypersensitivity reaction to doxorubicin hydrochloride, including anaphylaxis (§4)
doxorubicin.notes: Dosing §2.2: single agent 60-75 mg/m2 IV q21d; in combination 40-75 mg/m2 q21-28d; consider lower dose/longer interval for heavily pretreated, elderly or obese patients. Cumulative doses >550 mg/m2 associated with increased cardiomyopathy risk (§2.2). Table 1 prints only the percentages '50%' and '75%' under 'Dosage Modification' without saying 'reduce by' or 'of dose'; they are recorded as reductions because the higher-bilirubin row carries the larger figure - verify against the label before clinical use. §2.5 extravasation text says 'Immediately discontinue Doxorubicin Hydrochloride Injection' - this refers to stopping the running injection, so it is recorded without the DISCONTINUE keyword to keep it out of the permanent-stop list. This is the conventional (non-liposomal) product; pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is a different label (see OVCA labels.json).

cyclophosphamide.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE for injection, powder for solution [Baxter Healthcare Company], SPL v20, effectiveTime 20250624, published 2026-05-28, setid 591d9955-3d9c-4cdc-a308-2f1288376b9f
cyclophosphamide.label_indication: §1.1 malignant diseases incl. adenocarcinoma of the ovary and carcinoma of the breast; endometrial carcinoma not listed.

urinary outflow obstruction (§4)
cyclophosphamide.notes: §2 contains no AE-specific modification table and no discontinuation rule. §2.1: give adequate fluid during/immediately after administration to force diuresis (urinary tract toxicity); administer in the morning. Baxter is the legacy innovator (Cytoxan) manufacturer; no brand-name injection SPL is current.

medroxyprogesterone_acetate.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, PROVERA (medroxyprogesterone acetate) tablets [Pharmacia & Upjohn Company LLC (Pfizer)], SPL v27, effectiveTime 20260629, published 2026-06-30, setid a586be28-96af-4fed-a13f-9b94fd4c7405
medroxyprogesterone_acetate.label_format: non-PLR (old format) - no numbered sections, no dose-modification subsection
medroxyprogesterone_acetate.label_indication: INDICATIONS AND USAGE: 'treatment of secondary amenorrhea and abnormal uterine bleeding due to hormonal imbalance in the absence of organic pathology, such as fibroids or uterine cancer' and 'prevention of endometrial hyperplasia in nonhysterectomized postmenopausal women who are receiving daily oral conjugated estrogens 0.625 mg tablets'.
baseline_contraindications: undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding (CONTRAINDICATIONS 1)
known, suspected, or history of breast cancer (CONTRAINDICATIONS 2)
known or suspected estrogen- or progesterone-dependent neoplasia (CONTRAINDICATIONS 3)
active DVT, PE, or a history of these conditions (CONTRAINDICATIONS 4)
active arterial thromboembolic disease (e.g. stroke, MI), or a history of these conditions (CONTRAINDICATIONS 5)
known anaphylactic reaction or angioedema to PROVERA (CONTRAINDICATIONS 6)
known liver impairment or disease (CONTRAINDICATIONS 7)
known or suspected pregnancy (CONTRAINDICATIONS 8)
medroxyprogesterone_acetate.notes: The label's indications do NOT include endometrial cancer, and its DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION gives only 5-10 mg daily for 5-14 days per cycle; the 200-600 mg/day doses used for endometrial cancer appear nowhere in the label. The AUB indication is explicitly limited to bleeding 'in the absence of organic pathology, such as fibroids or uterine cancer'. CONTRAINDICATIONS item 3 ('Known or suspected estrogen- or progesterone-dependent neoplasia') read literally covers a progestin-treated endometrial cancer - EC use is off-label and the ranker should show this contraindication as a label caveat rather than a hard exclusion. No dose-modification or discontinuation rules in the label's D&A section. Warnings/Boxed Warning not extracted.
